statement: Heavier objects fall faster than lighter ones
why_wrong: In the absence of air resistance all objects accelerate downward at the same rate regardless of mass; the greater gravitational force on a heavier object is exactly cancelled by its greater inertia
real_world_consequence: Students mispredict the outcome of nearly every free-fall problem and distrust the result when they see it demonstrated

statement: A constant force produces a constant velocity
why_wrong: A constant net force produces a constant acceleration, not a constant velocity; constant velocity requires zero net force
real_world_consequence: Students cannot correctly read a velocity-time graph or predict motion under a steady push

statement: If an object is moving, there must be a force pushing it in the direction of motion
why_wrong: An object in motion continues at constant velocity with no net force at all; this is Newton's first law, and the intuition it displaces is the medieval impetus theory
real_world_consequence: Students invent forces that do not exist when drawing free-body diagrams

statement: An object at rest has no forces acting on it
why_wrong: A book on a table has both gravity and the normal force acting on it; they sum to zero, which is not the same as being absent
real_world_consequence: Students omit the normal force and get every equilibrium problem wrong

statement: In a collision, the heavier object exerts a greater force on the lighter one
why_wrong: The forces are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction by Newton's third law; the lighter object accelerates more because it has less mass, not because it is pushed harder
real_world_consequence: Students misanalyse every collision and cannot explain why a truck damages a car more than the reverse

statement: Heat and temperature are the same thing
why_wrong: Temperature measures the average kinetic energy of particles; heat is energy transferred between systems because of a temperature difference. A bathtub of warm water contains far more heat than a spark that is far hotter
real_world_consequence: Students cannot explain why a large cool object can melt more ice than a small hot one

statement: The seasons are caused by the Earth being closer to the Sun in summer
why_wrong: The seasons are caused by the tilt of the Earth's axis, which changes the angle and duration of sunlight; the Earth is in fact closest to the Sun in early January
real_world_consequence: Students cannot explain why the northern and southern hemispheres have opposite seasons at the same time

statement: Electric current is used up as it travels around a circuit
why_wrong: Charge is conserved: the current entering a resistor equals the current leaving it. What is used up is energy, not current
real_world_consequence: Students predict that a bulb nearer the battery will be brighter, and misread every series circuit

statement: The phases of the Moon are caused by the Earth's shadow falling on it
why_wrong: Phases are caused by which part of the sunlit half of the Moon faces the Earth as it orbits; the Earth's shadow on the Moon is a lunar eclipse, which is a different and much rarer event
real_world_consequence: Students cannot explain why a lunar eclipse is rare while a full moon happens monthly

statement: Astronauts float in orbit because there is no gravity in space
why_wrong: Gravity at the altitude of the space station is about 90% of its value at the surface; astronauts float because they and the station are in continuous free fall around the Earth
real_world_consequence: Students cannot explain what an orbit is, and treat weightlessness as the absence of a force rather than the absence of a support force
